about: Loader-change rules for modaccel convert, written for this project. Each rule says how one Fabric API use is written on NeoForge, and back. Nothing here was read from other people's mods: every class and member a rule names is checked against the loaders' own published jars by python bench/loader_api.py verify, which records where it found each one in coverage/loader/api.json. A rule's test is its before/after source; modaccel self-test runs every test both ways. Placeholders: $name matches one balanced Java expression; $event is the event object the listener receives; $modbus is the mod's own event bus.

entrypoints.about: fabric.mod.json main entrypoint (ModInitializer.onInitialize) <-> a @Mod class whose constructor runs onInitialize in NeoForge's first RegisterEvent, when every registry is open (GameData.unfreezeData runs before postRegisterEvents), so Registry.register calls work unchanged.

client entrypoint (ClientModInitializer.onInitializeClient, which Fabric runs once Minecraft exists and before its options load) <-> @Mod(dist = Dist.CLIENT) whose constructor runs it in RegisterKeyMappingsEvent at HIGHEST: NeoForge's first client event after Minecraft.instance is set, posted one priority phase at a time (ModLoader.postEvent), so key mappings it adds at normal priority still register.
server entrypoint (DedicatedServerModInitializer.onInitializeServer) <-> @Mod(dist = Dist.DEDICATED_SERVER) that runs it after the main entrypoint, in the first RegisterEvent at LOW priority.

fabric.mod.json <-> META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml: id, version, name, description, authors, license, contact, icon (iconFile from NeoForge 26.2, logoFile before), depends/recommends/suggests/breaks/conflicts <-> required/optional/incompatible/discouraged dependencies with Maven ranges, mixins <-> [[mixins]], access transformers <-> [[accessTransformers]].

fabric-datagen entrypoint (DataGeneratorEntrypoint.onInitializeDataGenerator(FabricDataGenerator)) <-> a method taking NeoForge's GatherDataEvent, called from a GatherDataEvent.Client listener the main @Mod class adds; pack.addProvider(X::new) <-> event.createProvider. Fabric's datagen bases wrap vanilla providers, so each provider class moves onto the vanilla one: FabricModelProvider -> ModelProvider(output, modId) with one registerModels calling generateBlockStateModels and generateItemModels; FabricBlockLootSubProvider -> BlockLootSubProvider over the mod's own blocks, inside a LootTableProvider; FabricRecipeProvider -> RecipeProvider.Runner; FabricAdvancementProvider -> AdvancementSubProvider inside an AdvancementProvider. The Loom datagen run becomes ModDevGradle's clientData run writing to the same folder. For Minecraft 1.21.4 to 26.2, where these providers take a PackOutput; 26.3 changed their constructors.

expressions.about: Fabric's FlammableBlockRegistry.add(block, burn, spread) fills the same two odds vanilla FireBlock.setFlammable(block, igniteOdds, burnOdds) keeps, in that order (Fabric's FireBlockMixin returns the first for getIgniteOdds and the second for getBurnOdds). NeoForge leaves setFlammable private, so the mod gets an access transformer for it; NeoForge 26.3 also reads a flammable data map.
Fabric's FabricCreativeModeTab.builder() is the builder NeoForge adds to CreativeModeTab itself (a no-argument CreativeModeTab.builder(), placing the tab after the vanilla ones).

expressions.about: Fabric's GameRuleBuilder.forBoolean(default).category(c).buildAndRegister(id) builds the GameRule vanilla's own GameRules.registerBoolean builds (BOOL type, bool() argument, Codec.BOOL, visitBoolean, 1 or 0 as the command result, no required features) and registers it under the mod's id; NeoForge mods register that GameRule themselves.
expressions.neoforge: Registry.register(BuiltInRegistries.GAME_RULE, $id, new GameRule<>($category, GameRuleType.BOOL, BoolArgumentType.bool(), GameRuleTypeVisitor::visitBoolean, Codec.BOOL, value -> value ? 1 : 0, $default, FeatureFlagSet.of()))

statements.about: Fabric registers default attributes at once; NeoForge collects them in EntityAttributeCreationEvent on the mod bus, which fires after registration.

integrations.about: Mod Menu (com.terraformersmc:modmenu) has no NeoForge build; NeoForge's own mod list opens a mod's config screen through IConfigScreenFactory. The ModMenuApi class keeps its factory as a Function<Screen, Screen>, and the client entry registers it.

bridges.about: For mods written for NeoForge first. NeoForge's registration (DeferredRegister and its holders), event bus (IEventBus, @SubscribeEvent, @EventBusSubscriber, NeoForge.EVENT_BUS), mod container, config (ModConfigSpec, read and written as the same TOML file), play payloads (PayloadRegistrar, PacketDistributor, IPayloadContext) and the commonest lifecycle events, written for this project on Fabric's API in knowledge/bridges/neoforge-on-fabric and copied into the converted mod beside its first @Mod class. Each class mirrors the NeoForge class named in classes (the members its symbols list), and each event is posted from the Fabric callback that fires at the same moment. @Mod constructors become Fabric entrypoints that receive their IEventBus and ModContainer from the bridge; registration runs at the end of the main entrypoint in the game's registry order, as NeoForge's RegisterEvent does.
